scope.authorization_statement: Ledgerly is a fictional application shipped with BoundaryLens and started on this machine. The operator owns it and may test it.
scope.note: Authorized scan of a developer-owned target. Findings and evidence are sanitized: no passwords, session tokens or authorization headers are included.

limitations: The scanner verifies the authorization rules declared in the manifest; it does not infer the application's complete business policy.
Confirmations are proven against seeded demo resources named in the manifest, not an exhaustive enumeration of every object.
Security-header and cookie items are hardening observations, interpreted for local HTTP development.

findings.title: Non-admin access to an administrator-only operation
findings.expected_rule: access limited to role 'admin'; owner is role:admin
findings.expected_behavior: Request denied (404/403) with no private resource data.
findings.severity_rationale: A non-administrator obtained administrator-only data, a privilege-boundary failure.
findings.remediation: Enforce a server-side role check on this operation before returning data; do not rely on the UI hiding it.
findings.limitations: Confirmed against the seeded demo resource named in the manifest. The scanner does not enumerate every object; other instances of the same route may share the defect.

findings.title: Anonymous access to a protected API resource
findings.expected_rule: access limited to the resource owner or role 'admin'
findings.expected_behavior: Unauthenticated request rejected with 401/403 (or redirected to sign-in).
findings.observed_behavior: HTTP 200 returned protected data without any session; response contains private marker(s) ['BLM-ALICE-ATT-7F3A']
findings.severity_rationale: Protected application data was served to an unauthenticated caller.
findings.remediation: Require a valid session for this route before returning data; ensure new routes inherit the same authentication guard as the rest of the API.
findings.limitations: Confirmed for the seeded resource/route in the manifest; not a full route inventory.

findings.title: Cross-user private-resource access
findings.expected_rule: access limited to the resource owner or role 'admin'; owner is alice
findings.expected_behavior: Request denied (404/403) with no private resource data.
findings.observed_behavior: HTTP 200; response contains private marker(s) ['BLM-ALICE-INV-7F3A'] and ownership field 'data.invoice.owner' = 'alice'
findings.severity_rationale: One ordinary user read another user's private record — a direct object-level authorization failure exposing confidential data.
findings.remediation: Check resource ownership server-side on every read (owner == caller or caller is admin); return 404/403 otherwise. Avoid trusting client-supplied object IDs.
findings.limitations: Confirmed against the seeded demo resource named in the manifest. The scanner does not enumerate every object; other instances of the same route may share the defect.

findings.title: Session not invalidated after logout
findings.expected_behavior: After logout the same session token is rejected (401/403).
findings.observed_behavior: After logout the reused session returned HTTP 200 with private marker(s) ['BLM-ALICE-INV-7F3A'], so the server-side session was not invalidated.
findings.severity_rationale: A logged-out session remains usable; a stolen/retained token keeps working, defeating logout.
findings.remediation: Invalidate the server-side session record on logout (delete it from the session store / rotate the identifier); do not merely clear the client cookie.
findings.limitations: Exercised with a dedicated throwaway session that does not touch the scanner's other test sessions.

findings.title: Security configuration observation
findings.severity_rationale: No CSP; reduced defense-in-depth against injection.
findings.limitations: Interpreted for local HTTP development: the Secure attribute and HSTS are not flagged over plain HTTP, and missing headers are treated as hardening observations, not access-control flaws.

findings.title: Security configuration observation
findings.route: Session cookie has no SameSite attribute
findings.observed_behavior: Session cookie has no SameSite attribute
findings.severity_rationale: No SameSite leaves the cookie exposed to cross-site request forgery in some browsers.
findings.remediation: Set SameSite=Lax (or Strict) on the session cookie.
findings.limitations: Interpreted for local HTTP development: the Secure attribute and HSTS are not flagged over plain HTTP, and missing headers are treated as hardening observations, not access-control flaws.

findings.remediation: Set HttpOnly on the session cookie.
